text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING eng-oncall - High streaming tail latency detected for gpu-pool-us-west-2. Alerts: p99 generation > 2s, streaming stalls increasing. Affected route: /v1/chat/stream. See dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/streams?orgId=1&var-pool=gpu-pool-us-west-2
eng-oncall: acknowledged. I'm on it. Can someone post recent grafana snapshots and any deploys in last 2 hours?
Samir: I see a spike starting ~08:41 UTC. p95 ~180ms, p99 ~2.3s, stall rate ~12% for streaming clients. CPU fallback is kicking in for some kernels.
Toni: infra-bot shows increased ECC correctable errors on node gpu-33 and thermal throttle events on gpu-35. Kernel messages look like repeated ECC_CE on pci 0000:af:00. Might be hardware flake.
Leah: Customer-impact: we have 3 paid customers reporting broken streaming sessions, some timeouts at 30s. SLA risk for 2 customers on Dedicated.
eng-oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) mark gpu-33 and gpu-35 unschedulable, 2) drain long-running streaming pods off those nodes, 3) route new streaming traffic to cpu-fallback pool + reduce batch size for fallbacks.
Samir: running drain now. Command:
```bash
kubectl cordon node/gpu-33
kubectl drain node/gpu-33 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30 --timeout=90s
```
Samir: drain started for gpu-33, evicting 6 streaming pods. One pod failed to delete due to GRPC hang, forcing restart.
Toni: started cordon/drain for gpu-35 as well. infra-bot: nvml shows temp spikes to 92C on gpu-35 and 85C on gpu-33, average power limit elevated. Thermal trips correlate with stalls.
Nate: enabling automated fallback routing for /v1/chat/stream to dedicated-fallback policy. Patch deployed: change route weight to fallback=0.25 for 10m.
eng-oncall: good. Also temporarily lower max_concurrent_streams to 8 for the affected pool to reduce KV cache thrash. Samir, can you confirm KV cache miss rates?
Samir: KV miss went from 4% to 18% during peak. After draining gpu-33 and gpu-35 miss dropped to 6% within 90s. p99 down to ~900ms.
Leah: Notifying account reps for the two impacted customers, opening INC-2026-0452 for tracking. ETA for node replacement? Toni?
Toni: We'll RMA gpu-35 if errors continue. Ops recommends a power cycling of server first to clear ECC sticky counters. ETA for RMA 48-72h.
infra-bot: powercycle request queued for host node-gpu-35 at 09:05 UTC.
eng-oncall: quick rollback options? Any kernel/driver updates rolled in last 6 hours?
Samir: no driver changes. There was a small runtime tweak to scheduling at 07:58 but it was feature-flagged; looks unrelated.
Nate: We've scoped affected customer sessions and applied 1-off reconnect hints to client library to resume streams gracefully.
Leah: I've updated incident doc with customer-facing note and current mitigation steps.
Toni: After the powercycle, NVML reports ECC CE count reset and temps stabilized ~78C. Streaming p99 now ~420ms, stalls <1%.
eng-oncall: marking incident as stabilized. Next steps: 1) replace GPU if CE counts reappear, 2) add node-level thermal alert thresholds to push earlier, 3) add runbook step to check ECC CE trend before high-latency paging.
Samir: I'll follow up with postmortem draft and perf traces. Assigning action items to ENG-ML for kernel heuristics evaluation.
Leah: Closing the page for now, keeping INC-2026-0452 open for postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
